dedupe_keys.name: bellinge data set urban drainage case study odense denmark

description: The Bellinge data set is an open benchmark for urban drainage research from a combined and separate sewer system serving the suburban towns of Brændekilde, Bellinge and Dyrup near Odense, Denmark, with a contributing area of about 1.72 square kilometres. It holds up to ten years of observations (2010 to 2020) from 13 level meters, one flow meter, one position sensor and four power sensors in the network, rainfall from three rain gauges and X- and C-band weather radars, and meteorological data, together with the asset database of manholes and pipes, drawings, CCTV inspection material, an orthophoto and terrain model, a catchment description, scripts and two uncalibrated hydrodynamic models of the system in MIKE URBAN and EPA SWMM. Researchers at the Technical University of Denmark and the utility VCS Denmark published it (Pedersen et al., Earth System Science Data, 2021) so that methods for calibration, data quality, machine learning, software sensors and digital twins can be tested and replicated on a common real system. Access: free download from the DTU Data repository as a collection of ten items (the sensor item alone is about 1.2 GB), under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: one small catchment only; the two models were not calibrated and differ systematically; the collection is a static release, last revised in 2023. Simulation uses: network flow model calibration and validation, benchmarking of real-time control and digital twins, and urban flood hazard studies. Related records: EPA SWMM (model-epa-swmm), which runs the supplied SWMM model.
